summary: Bidirectional alignment fails after a complete Q4 walk. The work request plus session-contract.md make the processor, CLI, schemas, lateness, restarts, and outputs discoverable, but several material contract rules are untested and one empty-input test is vacuous. A missing /tests/fixtures/empty.jsonl means the zero-event file case never runs; gap and max-duration closes do not require the triggering event to open the next session; journal-on-unchanged-watermark and raw negative journal values are unspecified in asserts; late-but-allowed last_event_time_ms, rejects truncation, and listed malformation classes can be skipped; omitted CLI args are graded as exit 2 without a stated code. Instruction shape and docs boundary are otherwise sound.

evidence.observation: Two paragraphs: incident plus repair of the existing Python processor; binding contract at /app/sessions/docs/session-contract.md; CLI /app/sessions/bin/run-sessions; knobs /app/sessions/config/processor.json; persist /app/sessions/data/watermark.journal and open-session state; outputs sessions.jsonl, late.jsonl, rejects.jsonl; leave /app/sessions/warehouse alone. Names unknown-flag fail-closed, --input tie-break vs --feed file order, --reset-output side-file wipe, event-time tenant/user half-open sessions, empty-input no watermark advance, and identical-run digests.

Binding CLI, paths, event/reject/late/session/journal/open-snapshot schemas, gap and max-duration close-then-open, watermark formula and compare-then-update order, late-but-allowed last_event_time_ms rule, per-observation journal including unchanged watermark_ms, raw negative journal values, --reset-output truncates rejects.jsonl, malformed classes, and forbidden Python/journal/contract rewrites.

Incident notes for mixed tenants on user_id=u1, late t=85000 classified on-time after a 100000 anchor, reset wiping watermark.journal, and seq stuck at 1. Points at the contract, CLI, warehouse, and /app/sessions/logs/processor-bounce.log.
Captured run evidence for journal rewrite, seq=1, f3/f4 classified on_time, --reset-output clearing the journal, and unknown flag still creating watermark.journal.
Public knobs session_gap_ms=30000, allowed_lateness_ms=10000, max_session_duration_ms=3600000; tests rewrite this file dynamically for gap/lateness/duration probes.
Public operator entry: bash wrapper exec python3 -m src.cli. Graded as the only supported CLI.

Operator CLI interface: unknown flags via argparse; missing source returns 2 after _touch_runtime; --reset-output currently clears journal in the inherited binary; missing --input path is treated as empty by read_events.
read_events returns empty events/rejects when the source path is not a file, so a missing empty.jsonl is observationally identical to a zero-event file on the inherited decoder.
Reachable catalog/ledger/ops plane writes /app/sessions/data/ops-report.json and desk/run metrics. Those paths are not named in instruction/contract and are not graded.

36 tests: 27 F2P + 9 P2P by name. Cover unknown flags, --empty-check, gap end_ms, --input sort, tenant isolation, journal seq/prefix/nondecreasing, too-late schema, malformed JSON and negative time, idempotent digests, restart, config mutations, holdout gap/tenant, tie-break by user, --feed order, reset keeps journal, watermark formula, warehouse hash, python3 launcher, and contract formula string. Do not assert close-then-open of the triggering event, per-observation unchanged journal lines, raw negative watermark_ms, last_event_time_ms after a late join, rejects truncation, or empty/missing/wrong-type ids.

Shipped hidden fixtures: feed_late.jsonl, feed_order.jsonl, holdout_sessions.jsonl, lateness_probe.jsonl, tie_break.jsonl. No empty.jsonl, though test_f2p_zero_event_file_no_journal_advance passes --input /tests/fixtures/empty.jsonl.

Public five-event sample used for gap close [1000,35000), tenant isolation, journal seq=5, and idempotent digests. Sorted event times all increase max_observed, so this fixture cannot distinguish journal-on-every-observation from journal-on-increase.
Classification-only: 27 F2P and 9 P2P labels. Used solely for F2P/P2P ownership, not as coverage authority.
Every stated requirement needs a meaningful assertion; every assertion must be discoverable from instruction plus referenced contracts; hidden tests may vary examples, not invent requirements.

PASS requires empty BLOCKING_FINDING_IDS after complete forward/reverse matrices, instruction/docs walks, F2P/P2P and output-interface walks, and a second omission sweep. Material untested requirements, phantoms, and grading-relevant ambiguities are REVISE.
Instruction owns the engineering ask; schemas/CLI/protocol may live in referenced docs; materiality of untested documented interfaces still blocks Q4.

findings.criterion: test_f2p_zero_event_file_no_journal_advance grades --input /tests/fixtures/empty.jsonl, but that fixture is not in tests/fixtures/ and is not copied by tests/Dockerfile.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires a zero-event input file to leave sessions/late empty without journal append. The test never presents an empty file. A missing path is treated as empty by the inherited decoder, so a file-not-found CLI (reasonable and stricter) fails while a missing-file-as-empty implementation passes. That is both vacuous coverage of the stated empty-file rule and a phantom success path for absent inputs.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add tests/fixtures/empty.jsonl (zero bytes or no event lines), copy it with the other fixtures, and keep the assertion on that real file. Do not treat a missing path as a successful empty batch unless the contract says so.
findings.regression_risk: Low if the new fixture is truly empty; high if Oracle currently depends on missing-file-as-empty.

findings.criterion: Gap and max-duration rules require close then open a new session at the triggering event_time_ms; tests only assert the closed first interval and allow the triggering event to be dropped.
findings.why_it_matters: sample_basic e3, unsorted z2, holdout h5, and duration d2 are the events that should start the next session. Current asserts check only the prior close (e1/e2, z1, h1-h3, d1). Dropping the triggering event still passes. That is incorrect observable session membership on a documented stable interface.
findings.minimal_remediation: After those fixtures, assert the triggering event_id is in a new open or subsequent closed session with start_ms equal to that event_time_ms, not in the just-closed interval.
findings.regression_risk: Low; tightens an already-stated close-then-open rule.

findings.criterion: Journal protocol requires one line per successfully parsed observation even when watermark_ms is unchanged, and raw (possibly negative) watermark_ms in the journal; tests never isolate either.
findings.why_it_matters: sample_basic under --input is strictly increasing max_observed, so seq==5 does not distinguish journal-on-increase. feed_late has non-increasing observations (f3, f4) but the nondecreasing test does not require five lines. First-event watermark_ms=-9000 is never asserted; formula check uses f1 at 80000 -> 70000. A journal that skips unchanged watermarks or clamps negatives to 0 still passes, violating the documented journal protocol the instruction forbids throwing away. MEDIUM blocks because it changes compliance with a documented stable public interface.
findings.minimal_remediation: On feed_late (or similar), assert journal line count equals successfully parsed events and that a non-increasing observation still appends. On an early event with event_time_ms < allowed_lateness_ms, assert journaled watermark_ms is the raw difference, not max(0, ...).
findings.regression_risk: Low; may fail implementations that already clamp or skip, which the contract already disallows.

findings.criterion: Late-but-allowed must update last_event_time_ms only when event_time_ms is greater; tests only check that f3 joins event_ids.
findings.why_it_matters: f3 at 85000 joins after last=100000, then f5 at 110000 overwrites last either way. Always-lowering last_event_time_ms is a plausible wrong join that still passes and can change later gap or watermark closes. MEDIUM blocks because it can change observable session intervals.
findings.minimal_remediation: Use a feed that ends on a late-but-allowed straggler (or snapshot immediately after f3) and assert last_event_time_ms remains the higher on-time timestamp while event_ids includes the straggler.

findings.criterion: --reset-output must truncate rejects.jsonl; test_f2p_reset_output_keeps_journal never asserts rejects are wiped.
findings.why_it_matters: The CLI contract lists rejects.jsonl with sessions.jsonl and late.jsonl as reset targets. The reset test starts from sample_basic (no rejects) then --reset-output --empty-check, so skipping rejects truncation still passes. That is an untested documented stable CLI interface and can change pass/fail once a reject-producing prior run is used.
findings.minimal_remediation: Seed rejects.jsonl, run --reset-output with a no-reject source or --empty-check, and assert rejects.jsonl is empty while journal and open_sessions.json are unchanged.

findings.criterion: Fail-closed malformed coverage only exercises invalid JSON and negative event_time_ms; missing fields, empty ids, wrong types, and empty-but-required payload are stated and untested.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract lists those malformation classes as rejects, not late, and says payload may be empty. An implementation that only rejects the two tested shapes would accept empty tenant_id or drop empty payload and still pass. That changes fail-closed observable correctness on a documented input schema. MEDIUM blocks.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add compact reject cases for missing field, empty id, wrong type, and accept one empty-payload valid event; keep them out of late.jsonl.

findings.criterion: test_f2p_missing_source_does_not_create_journal requires exit status 2 when --input/--feed/--empty-check are all omitted; the contract specifies exit 2 only for unknown flags.
findings.why_it_matters: A conforming CLI that prints usage and exits 1, or refuses to create a journal while exiting 1, fails this test. Instruction only requires unknown flags to fail before journal/output touch. Two competent readings diverge and the verifier accepts only exit 2. Grading-relevant ambiguity plus a phantom exit-code contract. MEDIUM blocks because it can change solver pass/fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Either state in the CLI contract that omitting --input/--feed/--empty-check is a usage error with exit 2 and no mutations, or grade only that the journal/outputs are untouched and accept conventional usage-error codes.
findings.regression_risk: Low if the contract is clarified to match the test; do not silently keep the hidden exit code.

findings.criterion: test_p2p_python_cli_entrypoint requires the substring python3 in bin/run-sessions rather than Python session logic.
findings.why_it_matters: A Python processor launched with python or a non-python3 token fails despite satisfying 'do not move session logic into another language'. Advisory launcher-token coupling, not a new functional rule.
findings.minimal_remediation: Assert the CLI still executes the Python package (for example python3 -m src.cli or equivalent) without making python3 the only legal token, or name python3 as the public launcher in the contract.

findings.criterion: test_p2p_warehouse_at_least_10k enforces len(lines) >= 10000, which is not a solver-visible count.
findings.why_it_matters: Leave-warehouse-alone is stated and also hashed after a run. The exact 10000 threshold is a hidden size for the inherited dump. A correct non-touching solution still passes, so this is advisory rather than a material phantom.
findings.minimal_remediation: Keep the post-run digest as the preservation check; treat 10k as an environment sanity assert or state that the inherited ledger must remain the shipped production dump.

findings.criterion: instruction.md never names /app/sessions/data/open_sessions.json even though tests read and write it.
findings.why_it_matters: Edition 3 asks instruction.md to name verifier paths. The binding contract does name the snapshot path and instruction already delegates restarts to that doc, so a fair solve is still possible. Advisory completeness, not a hidden requirement.
findings.minimal_remediation: Name /app/sessions/data/open_sessions.json once in the instruction persist sentence.

findings.criterion: Reject schema requires event_id null when the object has no string event_id; tests never assert that.
findings.why_it_matters: Malformed JSON in sample_late_and_reject.jsonl should emit event_id null. Tests only require REJECT_MALFORMED plus line_no/detail. Incidental field completeness relative to fail-closed behavior already graded.
findings.minimal_remediation: On the invalid-JSON line, assert event_id is JSON null.

findings.criterion: Crash-consistent snapshot (temp file then atomic replace) and UTF-8 JSONL without BOM are stated and untested.
findings.why_it_matters: Durability/encoding mechanics are hard to grade without a crash harness. Restart tests already require a reloadable snapshot. Advisory, not a pass/fail trap for a correct implementation.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: assert snapshot JSON parses after restart and files have no UTF-8 BOM. Do not add flaky kill -9 tests.

findings.criterion: Tie-break permutation only varies user_id; equal (tenant_id, user_id, event_time_ms) ordered by event_id is untested.
findings.why_it_matters: The (tenant_id, user_id) slice of the tie-break is graded. The event_id component is a finer ordering that current fixtures never collide on. Unlikely to change pass/fail for otherwise correct --input sorting.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: two same-key same-time events with swapped event_id order under --input.
